title: Coroner questions 'dynamic entry' raids
subtitle: Report cites two shooting deaths
article: A provincial coroner's report is raising new questions about the need for so-called dynamic entry police raids.
Coroner Luc Malouin was investigating the death of Yves Beauchamp, who was killed while exchanging gunfire with police who burst into his home during a pre-dawn raid.

According to the Sûreté du Québec, investigators were concerned Beauchamp would destroy evidence when they decided to enter his St. Sulpice home at 5:30 a.m. on June 14, 2006. He was under investigation for allegedly attempting to defraud the government through construction contracts. Police had information Beauchamp, 53, was often armed.
Malouin heard evidence from members of the tactical squad who burst into Beauchamp's home, saw him leave his bedroom and shouted: "Police! Get down on the ground!"
They heard a shot and returned gunfire. Beauchamp was shot in the head and died instantly. A member of the tactical squad was injured.
Beauchamp's spouse told Malouin her husband was startled awake by the noise of police bursting into their home. She said they were concerned about a recent home invasion in the area.
Comparisons to the 2007 death of Laval police Constable Daniel Tessier during a dynamic entry raid were not lost on Malouin.

Tessier was fatally shot by Basil Parasiris after Laval po- lice raided his Brossard home. During his first-degree murder trial, Parasiris and his wife testified they thought they were about to become the victims of a home invasion. Parasiris was acquitted.

"Did (Beauchamp) know it was the police? I don't believe it. It is possible the fact of being startled awake with the stress of a recent home invasion in the same neighbourhood caused the victim to act in an automatic way," Malouin wrote in a report obtained by The Gazette yesterday.
Malouin questioned "the pertinence of using this method when the danger involved is factored in."

He asked a former teacher at the École nationale de police de Québec for an independent opinion on dynamic entries. The teacher determined a dynamic entry was the safest alternative to secure evidence under the circumstances.

The coroner's bureau has yet to release its findings in Tessier's death. In October, the Commission de la santé et de la sécurité du travail, the provincial workplace health and safety board, criticized Laval police for not properly assessing the risk of entering Parasiris's home.

Malouin made one recommendation in his report: That the SQ use marked vehicles during dynamic entries and that their sirens and revolving lights be turned on after they smash in the door of the house being searched.
Sgt. Gregory Gomez Del Prado said the SQ would need time to analyze Malouin's report before commenting on it.
A spokesperson for Public Security Minister Jacques Dupuis said he would not comment on the report.
